title: Helpy: Dragonwilds Sync Field Guide
subtitle: A task-first visual guide to Worlds, DragonConnect, file Sync, servers, characters, mods, RSDW-L, Quick Launch, and recovery.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.summary: Install, launch, detect Dragonwilds, and create your first usable profile.
pages.intro: Dragonwilds Sync keeps Worlds, characters, mods, and launcher settings together without replacing Steam or the game.

sections.title: First launch
steps: Launch Dragonwilds Sync.exe on Windows or Dragonwilds Sync.AppImage on Linux. On Linux, mark the AppImage executable or add it through Gear Lever.
Keep Dragonwilds Sync Headless beside the normal application when you want profile-owned command-line server control or desktop Headless shortcuts.
Open Settings and confirm the detected Dragonwilds installation, save directory, and preferred launch provider.
Use Refresh Help if this guide was opened before the newest manifest downloaded.

sections.title: Create the first profile
steps: Open Worlds and choose Add World or import an existing local save.
Choose Singleplayer, Connected World, or Dedicated Server. Identical display names are allowed because profiles use independent internal IDs.
Add an icon, banner, description, and character assignment, then save the profile.

sections.title: Safe operating pattern
sections.body: Keep Steam Cloud disabled for saves managed by Sync, close the game before replacing save files, and use profile activation before launching so the correct mod set is staged.

tips: A Connected World needs only IP or hostname, World Name, and World Password.
Back up important saves before the first edit.

pages.title: Navigation & Appys
pages.summary: Understand the focused tools, global search, themes, notifications, and update controls.
pages.intro: Each Appy is a focused workspace. Permissions and profile context follow you between them.

sections.title: Core Appys
steps: Worlds manages singleplayer, Connected World, and server profiles.
Characters edits appearance, inventory, equipment, pose, and preview background.
Mods manages the shared repository plus profile-specific overrides.
Servers provides runtime, SteamCMD update, map, remote-user, and WebHost controls.
Helpy opens this same GitHub-managed guide in a focused in-app view.

sections.title: Search and themes
sections.body: The global search finds Appys, Worlds, characters, mods, Sync status, and help. Theme settings separate light or dark mode from the optional glass layer, including blur and stained-glass treatment.

sections.title: Safe application updates
steps: Application update checks compare the running package version with the latest GitHub release; the current version should not be offered to itself.
Choose Download Update to save the verified portable file in Downloads. Dragonwilds Sync remains open and never executes or replaces the file automatically.
Open the update receipt, copy its instructions if needed, close Dragonwilds Sync, replace the old portable file manually, and launch the replacement.
UE4SS, RuneSchema, RSDW, and dedicated-server updates remain separate operations with their own status and recovery controls.

pages.title: Worlds, Profiles & Local Sync
pages.summary: Build profiles, assign characters, activate mod sets, and use desktop quick launchers.
pages.intro: A profile is the durable identity for a World. Its presentation, connection details, character links, and selected mods travel together.

sections.title: Profile types
steps: Singleplayer profiles own or reference a local save.
Connected World profiles retain remote connection metadata and may share a display name with a local World.
Dedicated Server profiles control a server installation and runtime.

sections.title: Activate and launch
steps: Select a profile and review its RuneSchema, UE4SS, and PAK badges.
Activate it to stage the selected repository mods into the correct game directories.
Launch from the profile or use Send to Desktop to create an RSDWL quick launcher with the profile argument.

sections.title: Cloud-folder sync
sections.body: Optional local-file sync can target a folder already managed by OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, or another provider. Sync treats it as a normal local path; the cloud client handles transport.

tips: Click a mod badge to inspect the loaded mods for that profile.
Placard and horizontal layouts show the same profile collection.

pages.title: Connected Worlds & LAN Discovery
pages.summary: Connect by address, discover LAN hosts, receive metadata, and assign characters.
pages.intro: Connected Worlds use a simple game connection. Sync fingerprints are metadata identifiers, not login requirements.

sections.title: Direct connection
steps: Choose Add Connected World.
Enter the IP address or hostname, World Name, and World Password. No client/server hash is required.
Choose one of your characters. A character may be assigned to multiple Worlds.
Connect once to receive the host icon, banner, description, mod list, and other published metadata.

sections.title: LAN scan
steps: Keep both devices on the same local network and allow Dragonwilds Sync through the private-network firewall.
Run LAN Scan and wait for the host heartbeat or local service discovery response.
Select the discovered World, confirm its game address and password, then create the Connected World profile.

sections.title: Convert a profile
sections.body: A Connected World may be converted to Singleplayer or Dedicated Server when the required save or server paths are available. Conversion keeps presentation metadata while changing runtime ownership.

tips: NAT, VPN isolation, guest Wi-Fi, or a blocked UDP discovery port can prevent LAN discovery.
A heartbeat publishes status and presentation metadata, never a plaintext password.

pages.title: Sync Public World Directory
pages.summary: Find only Worlds actively broadcasting through Dragonwilds Sync and understand their live state.
pages.image_alt: Connected Worlds and public Sync discovery
pages.intro: The website World Directory is intentionally limited to verified Dragonwilds Sync heartbeats. It does not mix in general EOS, third-party, or gameplay-only server observations.

sections.title: Open the directory
steps: Choose World Directory from any website page or open the Public World Directory from Sync in the application.
Search by World name, region, tag, mod, or build.
Use All Broadcasting, Sync + Game Active, or Sync Only to narrow the live roster.

sections.title: Read the state
sections.body: SYNC + GAME ACTIVE means the World is heartbeating through Dragonwilds Sync and its Dragonwilds process is active. SYNC ONLY means the Sync service is still heartbeating while the game process is stopped, recovering, or waiting to start.

sections.title: What is public
sections.body: A host may publish presentation, classification, player totals, build, platform declarations, rules, mod summaries, and a safe public route. World passwords, Sync credentials, owner keys, administrative credentials, and private filesystem paths are never directory fields.

sections.title: When a World disappears
sections.body: The listing remains only while Cloudflare receives a current signed Sync heartbeat. Stopping the game does not hide a still-broadcasting Sync service; stopping or expiring the Sync heartbeat removes the World from the active website roster.

tips: A visible Sync-only World is not necessarily joinable until Dragonwilds becomes active.
The website and application use the same stable World identity even if the host public IP changes.

pages.title: Characters & Live 3D Preview
pages.summary: Edit appearance, colors, pose, background, equipment, inventory, and hotbar safely.
pages.intro: The Character Editor separates save-backed edits from preview rendering so repeated changes do not reload the model unexpectedly.

sections.title: Appearance
steps: Choose Appearance and edit face, hair, beard, body type, and color palettes.
Use the palette popup for skin, eyes, hair, or beard instead of narrow swatch rows.
Save the character record when the intended values are complete.

sections.title: Pose and background
steps: Open Pose to choose or filter an available stance.
Open Background to choose a solid color or one of the image thumbnails such as forest, beach, tavern, desert, or graveyard.
Backgrounds affect the preview stage only; they do not modify the game save.

sections.title: Preview refresh
steps: Make appearance, equipment, or hotbar changes without waiting for a renderer reload.
Click See Changes beside the character name when you want to rebuild the 3D preview.
Orbit, pan, and zoom after the model is ready. The renderer remains centered as the window changes size.

sections.title: Inventory interactions
sections.body: Right-click an equipment slot or hotbar slot for remove, change, and filtered repository actions. Drag compatible repository items into supported slots. Save only after checking item identity and stack count.

pages.title: Mods & Shared Repository
pages.summary: Import, fingerprint, classify, edit, and assign mods to profiles.
pages.intro: The shared mod repository stores a master copy while profiles select repository versions or maintain profile-specific overrides.

sections.title: Import and fingerprint
steps: Import an archive or scan a supported game/server mod directory.
Sync identifies RuneSchema, UE4SS, and PAK layouts and records an SHA-256 fingerprint.
A later rescan detects added, removed, or replaced payloads even when names are unchanged.

sections.title: Assign to profiles
steps: Open a mod placard and choose the target profiles.
Use the repository copy for shared maintenance or create a profile override when that World needs unique files or metadata.
Activate a profile to stage its exact selection into the game directory.

sections.title: Mod Editor paths
sections.body: The Mod Editor resolves each mod from its logical root. RuneSchema content is shown relative to RuneSchema/Mods/ModName, including assets, blueprints, raw data, and matching PAK content, rather than exposing unrelated server-root prefixes.

sections.title: ID.txt and hotload
sections.body: Metadata parsing accepts individual KEY = VALUE fields in any supported order. HOTLOAD = YES is valid by itself and marks supported edits as hotload-capable; unsupported payload changes still require restart.

tips: Recommended-mod placards link their Nexus Mods or Steam source icon directly to the listing.
Do not edit a staged profile copy when the repository master is the intended source.

pages.title: Item Repository & Spawner
pages.summary: Search vanilla and modded items, inspect identities, and grant items through controlled permissions.
pages.intro: The Item Repository combines the RSDW baseline with item manifests supplied by installed mods.

sections.title: Desktop use
steps: Open Item Spawner and choose the active server profile.
Filter by display name, internal name, Persistence ID, category, vanilla, modded, or unrecognized status.
Select an online player, item, and safe stack quantity, then confirm the grant.

sections.title: Remote use
steps: Grant the remote user View item repository to expose the Item Spawner Appy.
Grant Give / spawn items only to operators who may alter player inventory.
The catalog loads on demand; item grants are routed through the local RSDW service and written to the audit log.

sections.title: Modded items
sections.body: Mod manifests can add display names, internal names, Persistence IDs, runtime paths, stack limits, and icons. Rescan the repository after installing or replacing a mod so new item definitions appear.

pages.title: Dedicated Server Setup & Updates
pages.summary: Install with SteamCMD, configure runtime, monitor updates, and manage server mods.
pages.intro: Server Manager controls the local dedicated server. Public WebHost creation is a separate advanced feature.

sections.title: Install
steps: Create a Dedicated Server profile and choose an install directory.
Provide SteamCMD or let Sync detect it, then start installation.
Watch the status and progress text while Steam downloads, verifies, and applies the server build.
Configure World Name, World Password, ports, save path, and startup options.

sections.title: Operate
steps: Start, stop, or restart from Server Manager.
Use Update Server to compare installed and available build IDs and follow live SteamCMD progress.
Review health, players, logs, map bridge, and mod categories before launching clients.

sections.title: Server mod parity
sections.body: Server and singleplayer Mod Managers use the same RuneSchema, UE4SS, and PAK categories, icons, logical mod roots, and repository metadata. Server indexing is cached and refreshed only when files change.

pages.title: Remote Users, Login & Permissions
pages.summary: Create World-scoped accounts with individual passwords and least-privilege Appy access.
pages.intro: Each remote user has an independent password hash, one assigned World, and an explicit permission snapshot.

sections.title: Create an account
steps: Open the server profile, then Remote Access or Server Manager users.
Enter a unique username and a strong user-specific password. This is not the World Password and not the owner Admin Password.
Choose the exact World and enable only the required permissions.
Share the Server Admin URL, World selection, username, and that user's password through a secure channel.

sections.title: Permission groups
steps: Read permissions expose Overview, Map, Maintenance, Mods, Configs, Item Repository, Console, or Audit.
Write permissions allow maintenance changes, mod metadata, config saves, item grants, console commands, or broadcast messages.
Lifecycle permissions separately control Start, Stop, Restart, Update, and Refresh Metadata.

sections.title: Item Spawner and broadcasts
steps: View item repository displays the Item Spawner Appy; Give / spawn items enables grants to online players.
Send announcements displays Broadcast Messages and permits time-limited info, success, warning, or critical notices.
Both actions are validated by the desktop host and recorded in the remote audit log.

sections.title: Sign in and revoke
sections.body: The user selects the World, enters their username and their own password, then receives an eight-hour session with CSRF protection. Disable or delete the account to block future sign-ins; change its password if credentials may have leaked.

tips: Leave username blank only for the owner fallback that uses the server Admin Password.
Never reuse the World Password as a remote operator password.

pages.title: Server Manager, WebHost & Heartbeats
pages.summary: Choose the correct external surface and publish accurate World metadata.
pages.image_alt: WebHost preview and public World page
pages.intro: Remote Server Admin and public World hosting are separate surfaces. WebHost is advanced because it combines both.

sections.title: Remote Server Admin only
sections.body: Enable Server Manager remote access to publish only the authenticated login surface. The public directory and World placards remain disabled.

sections.title: WebHost
steps: Enable WebHost only when you want a public World page plus Server Admin entry.
Configure bind address, port, firewall profile, public transport, and Cloudflare or direct public URL.
Preview the external site and verify that passwords and private paths never appear in public metadata.

sections.title: Heartbeat metadata
sections.body: Heartbeat updates include a distinct Sync-broadcast state and Dragonwilds-process state plus players, game and Sync ports, icon, banner, description, platform, version, and mod badges/list. The public website lists only active Dragonwilds Sync heartbeats and labels Sync + Game Active separately from Sync Only.

sections.title: Troubleshoot publication
steps: Confirm the local directory host is running and bound to the intended interface.
Check firewall, tunnel, public URL, ingestion token, and heartbeat timestamp.
Use remote-only mode when public hosting is not desired; use full WebHost only after its preview is correct.

pages.title: RSDWL Launchers & Exchange Packages
pages.summary: Create desktop quick launchers and safely import or export validated package files.
pages.intro: A validated .rsdwl is the primary exchange path. Sync also accepts safely structured ZIP files and renamed .rsdwl compatibility archives so creators may keep their own nested folder layout.

sections.title: Validated .rsdwl — primary path
steps: Export from Dragonwilds Sync to create the package ID, manifest, payload index, sizes, SHA-256 hashes, provenance, and signature.
Creators may organize payload files in their own nested folders; the manifest maps those safe relative paths for Sync.
Import the .rsdwl directly. Sync validates it before reading or applying any profile, World, character, or mod records.

sections.title: Desktop launcher
steps: Choose Send to Desktop on a World or server profile.
Sync writes an RSDWL launcher that carries the profile identifier as a quick-launch argument.
Open it to activate the profile, stage its mods, and launch the intended client or server flow.

sections.title: ZIP and custom-folder compatibility
sections.body: As a secondary path, the importer recognizes ordinary mod ZIPs and manually renamed .rsdwl ZIP containers. It walks nested members, normalizes an extra top-level folder and legacy layouts, rejects unsafe paths, then identifies RuneSchema, UE4SS, or PAK payloads without requiring creators to flatten their folders.

sections.title: Safety
sections.body: Do not trust extension renaming alone. Sync rejects traversal paths and inspects manifests, package types, hashes, signatures, payload indexes, and known metadata before applying records.

pages.title: File Sync, Transfer & Diagnostics
pages.summary: Understand the separate Sync service, authenticate, transfer required files, and read acknowledgements.
pages.intro: Dragonwilds game announcement and Dragonwilds Sync file transfer are independent processes. The game port launches play; the Sync endpoint verifies identity and transfers only the files the selected profile requires.

callout.title: Know which connection failed
callout.body: Game UDP 7777, Direct discovery UDP 8422, and Sync transfer TCP 27051 serve different jobs. A working game announcement does not prove the file-transfer listener is reachable.

sections.title: Connection sequence
steps: Discover or enter the host, then save one Connected World profile.
Resolve a LAN or external route and verify the advertised World fingerprint.
Authenticate the Sync session with the World policy, receive the manifest, and compare local fingerprints.
Transfer required differences and verify hashes. The ready window then shows copyable World Name, Direct Connect address, and plain-text World Password for manual entry.

If the server opted into DragonLink-Connect, open the in-game Direct Connect panel and its fields are filled once for that panel visit. Otherwise enter the same receipt manually, then press Play when ready.

sections.title: What the progress window means
sections.body: The movable connection window reports route selection, challenge response, manifest receipt, individual file transfers, hash checks, client acknowledgement, host acknowledgement, and launch handoff. Closing it dismisses the view; it does not silently mark a failed step successful.

sections.title: Diagnostic text export
sections.body: When diagnostics are enabled, Sync writes a redacted TXT report to Downloads for both successful and failed attempts. It includes timestamps, selected route, ports, stages, transfers, acknowledgements, and the first authoritative failure without writing plaintext passwords or reusable secrets.

sections.title: Connection refused
steps: Confirm Sync Hosting is running and bound to 0.0.0.0 or the intended LAN interface—not only 127.0.0.1.
Confirm TCP 27051 is not already occupied and the host firewall allows it.
For remote clients, forward TCP 27051 or use the configured tunnel. UDP 8422 is discovery only and does not carry mod files.
Retry from the saved Connected World so the refreshed route is retained instead of creating a duplicate profile.

tips: LAN discovery may waive an extra Sync challenge only when the host verifies the source as local and its policy allows that path.
World Password is a game credential; remote Server Management users have separate passwords.

pages.title: Quick Launch
pages.summary: Create movable, profile-aware launchers for local Worlds, Connected Worlds, and dedicated servers.
pages.intro: Quick Launch is a compact window over the same profile and lifecycle authority as the full application. It does not create a second compatibility layer or a second copy of a World.

sections.title: Create a launcher
steps: Open a local, Connected, or server World profile.
Choose Send to Desktop and select the player, co-op, or server launch mode.
Open the generated shortcut; its stable profile ID selects the intended World even when display names match.

sections.title: Player flow
sections.body: The compact player window verifies the saved route, runs required file Sync, stages the profile mod set, and starts Dragonwilds. Open Full Dragonwilds Sync is always available for details or corrections.

sections.title: Server flow
sections.body: The movable server window shows authoritative lifecycle state, players, update state, heartbeat, and Start, Stop, Restart, Update, and Update & Restart actions. Closing the application terminates launcher-owned helper processes.

sections.title: A shortcut opens the wrong profile
sections.body: Delete and recreate shortcuts made before the profile received its stable ID. A valid shortcut targets the profile ID, not the visible World name, IP address, or card position.

pages.title: Core Configuration & RuneSchema Flavors
pages.summary: Edit only core loader/game configuration and manage named RuneSchema runtime flavors safely.
pages.intro: Configuration is intentionally narrower than Mod Management. It exposes the UE4SS root config, the active RuneSchema root config, and Dragonwilds client/server configuration—not every file found inside installed mods.

sections.title: Configuration groups
steps: Expand UE4SS for its root configuration.
Expand RuneSchema for the selected flavor's root config.json.
Expand Game for normal-install settings or DedicatedServer.ini on a hosted World.
Use Mod Management when editing an individual mod's files.

sections.title: Named RuneSchema flavors
steps: Import a RuneSchema ZIP through the flavor manager and give it a clear name.
Select that flavor in the World profile; the placard and World details should show the same name.
Apply it before launch. Sync stages the payload into the canonical RuneSchema folder without changing its required runtime paths.

sections.title: Manual override
sections.body: A local unreleased RuneSchema build may be selected as an explicit manual override. Launch accepts the installed files without silently restoring the official release. Restore Official returns to the upstream GitHub runtime.

sections.title: Access denied while replacing a DLL
steps: Stop Dragonwilds, the dedicated server, and every launcher-owned bridge using RuneSchema.
Apply the flavor again after the process releases main.dll and related files.
If the file remains locked, use the visible process detail or diagnostic report; do not delete the whole runtime tree while it is active.

pages.title: Settings Reference
pages.summary: Find application, network, storage, advanced, integration, update, and about controls.
pages.intro: Settings now keeps machine-wide controls together and leaves profile-owned mods, World rules, and server runtime controls in their owning workspaces.

sections.title: Application, Network, Storage
sections.body: Application selects the game installation and launch behavior. Network controls discovery and client evidence. Storage explains APPDATA ownership, isolation, backups, and persistent runtime cores.

sections.title: Runtime & Data channels
sections.body: UE4SS and RuneSchema each provide Official and Experimental controls. UE4SS Experimental resolves the experimental-latest release tag. RuneSchema Experimental resolves the newest published release from gh0sted5456-us/RuneSchema, including prereleases, and labels it as testing current RuneSchema fixes and features.

sections.title: Stored build libraries
sections.body: Resolved builds retain version, nickname, publication date, source, and local archive. Select one or several stored copies to reapply or delete; World-specific manual ZIP overrides remain explicit and profile-scoped.

sections.title: Advanced
sections.body: Advanced switches opt optional hosting and remote surfaces into the application. Disabling a surface preserves its profiles and does not silently start or stop an unrelated service.

sections.title: Integrations
sections.body: Optional integrations such as Nexus Mods and Discord Rich Presence remain independent of local Worlds and dedicated-server operation. Rich Presence uses the selected profile and current activity without publishing credentials or private paths.

sections.title: What is intentionally absent
sections.body: Mod Management is not duplicated under Settings. World-owned mods live with the World; the shared repository lives in Mods; server installation and runtime cores live under Sync Hosting or the server profile.

pages.title: Troubleshooting & Recovery
pages.summary: Resolve connection, renderer, mod indexing, remote access, update, and shutdown problems.
pages.intro: Start with the smallest affected layer: profile, local service, network, remote surface, then external transport.

sections.title: Connected World missing
steps: Search by profile type as well as display name; local and Connected profiles may share a name.
Confirm IP or hostname, game port, World Name, and World Password.
For LAN discovery, verify private-network firewall access and disable guest-network client isolation.

sections.title: Mods or icons missing
steps: Rescan the correct game or server root.
Check that the logical mod root contains the expected RuneSchema, UE4SS, or PAK payload.
Refresh repository metadata so fingerprints, badges, custom items, and icons are rebuilt.

sections.title: Remote login rejected
steps: Confirm Remote Server Admin is enabled for that profile.
Select the assigned World and enter the account username plus that user's password, not the World Password.
Check that the account is enabled and has not been deleted or reassigned.

sections.title: AppImage will not close
sections.body: Wait for active save or server operations to finish, use the application Exit command, and inspect the latest log if shutdown stalls. Gear Lever integration should use the packaged Sync icon and desktop entry.

sections.title: Application update repeats or closes
steps: Confirm About reports the same version as the latest GitHub tag. Current tagged builds stamp that exact version into the package.
Use Download Update and wait for the verified receipt; the application should remain open.

If an older build closes itself, download Dragonwilds Sync directly from GitHub Releases, close the old launcher, and replace it manually. Future builds no longer self-replace or execute downloaded files.

sections.title: Get diagnostic context
sections.body: Record the profile type, operation, visible status message, timestamp, application version, operating system, and relevant log excerpt. Remove passwords, tokens, public IPs, and personal paths before sharing.

tips: Use Refresh Metadata before assuming cached presentation data is lost.
A failed external heartbeat does not prevent local server management.
